hens_rule_text: Up to 8 fowl per parcel are allowed by right, based on a density rule of 1 fowl per 4 sq ft of indoor coop space and 10 sq ft of outdoor space; more than 8 requires a Small Farm Animal Permit and extra land.
permit_notes: No permit needed for 8 or fewer fowl. Keeping more than 8 requires a Small Farm Animal Permit from the Health Commissioner, plus at least 20,000 sq ft of contiguous land and living within a quarter mile of the property.
setback_notes: Coop or cage must be at least 10 ft from structures and neighboring buildings.
coop_rules: Covered, predator-proof, ventilated coop, easy to access and clean, at least 2 sq ft of interior space per bird; coop and run together should not exceed about 50 sq ft.
zoning_notes: Allowed in residential zones under Ordinance 70608 (2017); non-residential zones are not covered by this residential-keeping rule.
hoa_note: Homeowners associations, deed restrictions and leases can be stricter than city law. Check yours before getting chickens.

research_notes: Facts come from search-result extracts of the city's own ordinance page and animal laws page plus a nonprofit's plain-language overview of the same ordinance; the full ordinance text could not be opened directly from this machine. No 2023 to 2026 amendment was found. State law (Missouri) does not set a hen cap; a 2024 HOA protection law was later struck down in court, so HOAs may still restrict chickens.
